snippet.title: Turning a Dusty Farm Find Into a Hollywood Car | Outback Car Hunters
snippet.description:
Deep in the Western Australian outback, Dave and GT uncover one of the most outrageous barn finds they've ever seen—a massive 1958 Chrysler Imperial Crown nicknamed "The Batmobile." Hidden away on a remote sheep farm, this rare American luxury cruiser is a relic from the golden age of oversized chrome, tailfins, and V8 power.

After striking a deal for just $8,000, the team faces a challenge: can they transform this giant forgotten classic into a desirable collector's car without blowing the budget?

But that's not the only treasure they discover. While hunting through paddocks filled with rusting relics, they stumble across a classic 1989 Range Rover and a collection of iconic Australian muscle cars, including a legendary Ford Falcon hardtop made famous by Mad Max.

With tight budgets, mechanical surprises, and plenty of laughs along the way, Dave and GT must work fast to bring these neglected classics back to life and turn a profit.

Will the Chrysler Imperial become the stunning American beauty it once was? And can the old Range Rover prove it's still fit for royalty?

Join Outback Car Hunters for another incredible adventure packed with rare barn finds, classic car restorations, epic negotiations, and unforgettable outback discoveries.

snippet.title: Holy Grail Combi Found in the Outback | Outback Car Hunters
snippet.description:
A helicopter search over the Australian Outback leads Dave and GT to one of the most shocking Volkswagen discoveries they've ever seen—a rare split-screen VW Combi that's been transformed into something unrecognizable.

Hidden deep on a remote cattle station, the legendary Kombi has been butchered, stripped, and converted into a trailer. But despite the missing parts, bullet holes, and decades of neglect, the pair see potential in what could be the ultimate restoration project.

Meanwhile, another lead uncovers a stunning red Mercedes-Benz SL Roadster, a Hollywood icon that once starred in some of the biggest TV shows of the 1970s and 1980s. With a tight deadline and thousands of dollars in repairs looming, Dave and GT race against the clock to transform the luxury convertible into a profitable flip.

From helicopter searches and outback car graveyards to rare parts hunts and high-stakes negotiations, this episode delivers incredible barn finds, classic car restorations, and unforgettable Australian adventures.

Will the holy grail Combi become a money pit, or can Dave and GT bring it back from the brink?

snippet.title: Air Crash Investigation - Concorde: Up In Flames (S14E07) - [FULL EPISODE]
snippet.description:
Air France Flight 4590 was an international charter flight from Paris to New York. On 25 July 2000, a Concorde passenger jet operating that flight crashed shortly after takeoff, killing all 109 people on board and 4 on the ground. Whilst taking off from Charles de Gaulle Airport, Air France Flight 4590 ran over debris on the runway dropped by an aircraft during the preceding departure, causing a tyre to explode and disintegrate. Tyre fragments, launched upwards at great speed by the rapidly spinning wheel, violently struck the underside of the wing, damaging parts of the landing gear – thus preventing its retraction – and causing the integral fuel tank to rupture. Large amounts of fuel leaking from the rupture ignited, causing a loss of thrust in the left side engines 1 and 2. The aircraft lifted off, but the loss of thrust, high drag from the extended landing gear, and fire damage to the flight controls made it impossible to maintain control. The jet crashed into a hotel in nearby Gonesse two minutes after takeoff.

snippet.title: Surviving Earth's Most Extreme Climates (Full Episode) | Hostile Planet: Compilation | Nat Geo
snippet.description:
Hosted by Bear Grylls, Hostile Planet zooms in on the world’s most extreme environments to reveal the animal kingdom’s epic stories of survival on this fast-changing and continuously evolving planet. In this Hostile Planet compilation from National Geographic, discover the animals that call deserts and the Earth’s poles home. 

Surviving the Desert - 0:00
How do animals survive in the desert? Desert wildlife relies on specialized adaptations to combat extreme heat, dehydration, and a lack of shade where the sun is the ultimate enemy. For desert animals like the Nubian ibex, Arabian wolf, and brown hyena, to survive in the desert means learning how to deal with the sun’s unrelenting volatility. 

Polar Habitats - 0:47:07
Polar habitats are similarly enslaved by the sun: half the year is plunged into bitterly cold darkness and hardship, and the other half is blistered with light and heat. What animals live in polar habitats? Polar regions are home to highly resilient species like polar bears, Arctic wolves, emperor penguins, musk ox, and more that are uniquely built to survive months of freezing darkness and sudden seasonal shifts. As the sun exerts its unquestionable dominance, we reveal the incredible ways these wild animals survive.

snippet.title: How a Retired American Airlines Pilot Landed a Vintage Seaplane on 7th Street
snippet.description:
Phoenix Seabee Crash,: The 2-Minute Emergency Landing That Saved Everyone on 7th Street

In this video, we break down the terrifying emergency landing of Republic RC-3 Seabee N6518K, a 1946 vintage amphibious aircraft that crash-landed on 7th Street in central Phoenix on April 12, 2026.

The sky was clear.
The winds were light.
The flight was supposed to be a short Sunday loop over the city.

Nothing about the afternoon looked dangerous.

Yet just minutes after takeoff, the aircraft’s engine began to fail over one of the worst possible places to lose power, downtown Phoenix.

There was no open field below.
No runway within reach.
No safe airport glide path.

Only buildings, traffic lanes, power lines, street signs, and a narrow city street that might or might not be clear by the time the airplane reached it.

How does a 79-year-old aircraft lose its engine over a crowded city?
And how did the pilot manage to land it on a public road without hitting a single car or pedestrian?

📚 Related Videos

Emirates Flight Investigation: https://youtu.be/1zdtquGc7wQ

Singapore Airlines: https://youtu.be/xZLOg0XybIY

South Korean Airline Flight Disaster: https://youtu.be/lOeiTgP2Tpk

✈️ The Story

On April 12, 2026, veteran pilot Mike Tragars took off from Hangar Haciendas in Laveen, south of Phoenix, for what should have been a simple sightseeing flight.

Onboard were two passengers, Hanan Haskell and Dragisa Raiche, both connected to aviation.

The aircraft was a Republic RC-3 Seabee, a rare amphibious aircraft built in 1946. It had a boat-shaped hull, a high-mounted rear engine, and a pusher propeller behind the cabin.

It was not a modern aircraft.
No advanced glass cockpit.
No modern automation to protect the crew.
No easy way for the pilot in the front to see what was happening behind him.

For the first few minutes, everything looked routine.

The aircraft climbed over the Phoenix Valley and leveled at around 2,500 feet. But then, the engine RPM began to surge. The sound changed. The pilot tried the controls, but the engine did not respond.

Moments later, one of the passengers noticed smoke coming from the rear-left side of the aircraft.

Then the smoke moved forward.

Then the engine quit completely.

At that point, Sky Harbor was no longer reachable. Neither were Deer Valley, Goodyear, Falcon Field, or any other airport in the valley.

The airplane was coming down inside the city.

With only minutes of altitude left, Tragars scanned the streets below and saw one possible option: 7th Street, between Missouri Avenue and Coulter Street.

By pure timing, the stretch directly ahead was almost empty.

He committed to the road.

The landing gear stayed retracted to help the aircraft slide and stop faster. The Seabee cleared one set of power lines by roughly 40 feet, passed beneath a street sign, touched down on the pavement, struck a fire hydrant, and slid to a stop near the curb.

🔎 The Investigation

The NTSB opened its investigation after the accident and recovered a 360-degree camera mounted on the aircraft’s right wing.

That footage captured the final two minutes and ten seconds of the flight in remarkable detail.

Investigators found that the engine’s exhaust tailpipe had separated from the manifold during flight. That failure caused thermal damage to nearby components and additional fractures in the exhaust system.

But the outcome was not just luck.

Tragars recognized the emergency quickly.
He stopped trying to reach an airport once the math no longer worked.
He selected the best available surface.
He kept the airplane under control.
And he executed a belly landing with almost no room for error.

This accident shows how fast a routine flight can turn into an urban survival problem, and how experience, timing, and decision-making can make the difference between a fatal crash and everyone walking away.

• Full timeline of the Phoenix Seabee emergency landing
• What happened to Republic RC-3 Seabee N6518K
• Why Phoenix is dangerous for engine failures
• Who pilot Mike Tragars was
• Why Sky Harbor was no longer reachable
• How 7th Street became the only landing option
• The final two minutes captured on wing camera
• Why the landing gear stayed retracted
• What the NTSB preliminary investigation found
• Key aviation safety lessons from the accident

This video is created for educational and documentary purposes based on official reports, public footage, and publicly available information.
